study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the screening arm of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Serum selenium in prospectively collected samples was compared between 724 incident prostate cancer case subjects and 879 control subjects, frequency-matched for age, time since initial screen, and year of blood draw.
reason: The nested case-control study evaluated incident prostate cancer overall using prospectively collected serum. No aggressive incident endpoint is established in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Overall, serum selenium was not associated with prostate cancer risk (P for trend = 0.70);
estimate_classifications.reason: The full-text estimate is explicitly labeled overall, and the abstract establishes that the outcome was incident prostate cancer without an aggressive subtype.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: higher serum selenium was associated with lower risks in men reporting a high (more than the median: 28.0 IU/d) vitamin E intake [odds ratio (OR) for the highest compared with the lowest quartile of selenium: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.37, 0.91; P for trend = 0.05; P for interaction = 0.01]
estimate_classifications.reason: This is a subgroup estimate for overall incident prostate cancer, not aggressive disease.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
